<!--
Thank you for your contribution to samurai!

Before opening the PR:
- Run the whole pre-commit suite (https://pre-commit.com/): `pre-commit run --all-files`.
- Title: conventional commits (https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/),
  `type(scope): summary`, imperative, lower case, no final period.
  Types: build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test.

How to write the description (people and AI agents alike):
- Write for a reviewer who knows samurai but not this change. Most PRs need 5 to 20 lines.
- State facts: the problem, the change, the evidence. Name functions, files, demos,
  command-line options and error messages exactly, in backticks.
- Give results as numbers, tables or before/after comparisons, not adjectives.
- Leave out: the list of changed files (the diff shows it), the steps or dead ends
  that led to the change, a restatement of the title, claims such as "improves
  readability" or "more robust" without evidence, and any mention of the tool or
  agent that wrote the change.
- Delete a section that does not apply, and delete these comments.
-->

## Description
<!--
What was wrong or missing, and what the PR changes.
- fix: the symptom as a user hits it (command, error message, wrong value), the cause, the fix.
- feat: what a user can now do, with a short code example if the API changes.
- refactor/perf: what changes in the code structure or the timings; say whether results change.
-->

## Related issue
<!-- `Closes #123`, or where the problem was found (issue, PR, CI job). -->

## How has this been tested?
<!--
- New or changed tests: name, what they check, and whether they fail without this PR.
- Demos or commands run, with their options (MPI processes, levels, final time...).
- What was not tested, and why.
-->
